messages:
leo (Customer): Hey team — our app started getting lots of 429s on our Dedicated pool rp-123 around 09:12 UTC, and some requests also returned intermittent 403s. Latency jumped from ~40ms to 600-1,200ms during spikes. Billing dashboard also shows a jump in hosted endpoint usage around the same time. Can you help triage?

anna (Support): Sorry you're seeing that — can you paste a few request IDs and any X-RateLimit headers from the responses? Also confirm your account id and pool id (you mentioned rp-123).

leo (Customer): account: acct-9876, pool: rp-123. Example response headers from a failing request: 
```
HTTP/1.1 429 Too Many Requests
X-Request-Id: req_0a1b2c3d
X-RateLimit-Limit: 100
X-RateLimit-Remaining: 0
X-RateLimit-Reset: 1680005600
X-Redwood-Pool: rp-123
```
Body: {"error":"rate_limited","message":"reserved pool exhausted"}
Also saw a 403 earlier: `{
  "error": "auth_failed",
  "message": "token rejected"
}` but those were <1% of traffic.

anna (Support): Thanks — that looks like the token-bucket exhausted. Two parallel asks: 1) I'll open an infra escalation to check pool/token config. 2) Can you run one quick header-capture on a failing request and paste the full raw response (including X-Redwood-* headers)? We want the X-Redwood-Behind and any fallback headers.

maria (Oncall): +1. I'm seeing a correlated deploy at 08:58 UTC that changed reserved-pool token-window from 60s -> 15s for some customers (canary). If that rolled into the region where rp-123 is, it would make bursts exhaust much faster and then fallback to shared endpoints (hence billing spike).

sam (Infra): Confirmed — canary:deploy/2025-06-12T08:58:12Z toggled pool config flag `short_burst_window=true` for eu-west-1 canary group. We didn't intend to include reserved pools in that canary, looks like rp-.* pattern matched too broadly. Rolling back now.

deploy-bot: canary:deploy/2025-06-12T08:58:12Z rollback started by sam — job 4456 queued.

leo (Customer): Ugh — that matches timing. What should we do to repro so we can confirm once rollback completes? Also how do we avoid this from affecting our SLA?

maria (Oncall): Repro steps to observe the problem locally:
1) Run a short burst load against your pool endpoint with a client ID header so the router attributes correctly:
```
wrk -t4 -c200 -d30s -H "Authorization: Bearer <YOUR_KEY>" -H "X-Client-ID: acct-9876" http://api.redwood.test/v1/generate
```
2) Watch for the X-RateLimit-Remaining header dropping to 0 quickly and then responses that include `X-Redwood-Fallback: shared` (those indicate fallback to hosted).

Also check pool settings with our internal CLI (we can run this for you if you want):
```
rictl pools get rp-123 --fields=name,capacity,qps,burst_multiplier,token_window
# expected: token_window=60, burst_multiplier=2 (if roll back applied)
```
If token_window is 15, that's the culprit.

sam (Infra): Mitigations while rollback finishes:
- We can temporarily bump rp-123 burst_multiplier to 4 (gives more headroom).
- Add an explicit routing rule to keep acct-9876 pinned to dedicated capacity (prevents fallback to hosted).
- If you have high-priority traffic, we can whitelist a subset of keys to bypass rate-limiter for short period.

anna (Support): I'm going to request the temporary bump + pinning now. Also opening a billing review; the spike likely from fallback to hosted endpoints which are billed differently. We'll track credits if this was caused by our deploy.

leo (Customer): Please do — we have a promo running and can't incur extra hosted charges. Thank you.

deploy-bot: rollback/4456: success at 09:06:41 UTC

sam (Infra): Rollback completed. Pool rp-123 token_window reverted to 60. I ran a quick check:
```
rictl pools get rp-123 --json
# {"name":"rp-123","capacity":1200,"qps":100,"burst_multiplier":2,"token_window":60}
```

maria (Oncall): After rollback we recommend you run the earlier wrk test again to validate. If you still see `X-Redwood-Fallback: shared`, paste the request IDs and we'll dig deeper.

anna (Support): Next steps for us:
- We've created INC-5543 (priority P1) for infra to audit canary targeting rules and to add an exclusion for reserved pools.
- Billing team looped in for credit assessment: BLG-1021.
- Support will keep this thread open until you confirm recovery.

leo (Customer): Ran the repro after rollback — traffic looks stable, no more 429s after a couple minutes. Thanks for the fast turnaround. Appreciated the temporary pin/rollback.

anna (Support): Glad it's resolved. We'll follow up with the incident write-up and any credits. Closing after we share the postmortem. :thumbsup:
